key_insight: Orienting the salt gradient changes where colloids are extracted from porous media: solute-out favors peripheral removal, while solute-in drives extraction from the stagnant core, and diffusioosmotic slip boosts both.
engineering_relevance: Controlling phoretic and osmotic transport in porous structures could improve membrane filtration, laundry detergency, and enhanced oil recovery.
method: 2D porous medium modeled as hexagonally packed pillars/fibers with equal spacing
Finite-element simulations of colloid transport under ambient flow and electrolyte gradients
Compared solute-out (emitting) versus solute-in (consuming) gradient orientations with/without diffusioosmotic slip
evidence_signal: Simulation results show qualitatively distinct extraction patterns for the two gradient orientations, with diffusioosmotic slip further amplifying extraction and giving a larger gain in the solute-in case.
watch_item: The study is simulation-based, so real porous-media performance may depend on pore-scale geometry, chemistry, and flow conditions not fully captured here.
paper_title: Colloid recovery from porous structures under ambient flow: enhanced extraction via phoretic and osmotic mechanisms
